transcript.text: I need to flag a constraint before we proceed. While tracing an unrelated build failure this morning, I found that six active release branches still fetch packages by legacy-registry coordinates: payments-v3, mobile-android-2025.06, mobile-ios-2025.06, desktop-4.8, analytics-2.3, and edge-agent-1.9. A July 31 hard shutdown would break those branches, so they need read-only compatibility access until their releases complete. I haven't updated the retirement ticket yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a privacy constraint on the registry-log handling workstream. During a privacy review of registry telemetry this afternoon, I confirmed that the access logs retain bearer-token fragments. That means the logs must have token fragments redacted and be purged after exactly 14 days, not the 90-day retention called for in the draft plan. I haven't opened the privacy finding yet, but this needs to be reflected in the retirement plan before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a customer artifact access constraint. I confirmed with the account team today that Harbor Health's contract requires downloadable access to its registry artifacts for 730 days after registry retirement. This was found during a customer-renewal review and hasn't been attached to the platform ticket yet. A July 31 hard shutdown of read access would violate Harbor Health's contractual artifact access rights, so the retirement plan needs to account for extended downloadable access for that customer before Riley approves.

Attach Harbor Health's 730-day contractual artifact access requirement to the platform ticket and ensure extended downloadable read access for Harbor Health artifacts is provisioned before legacy write access is shut off.

Write access will be shut off on July 31 as planned. Read access will remain available via allowlist for the six flagged release branches until release completion and for Harbor Health artifacts for 730 days post-retirement.
